newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hilton to pursue Asia-Pacific expansion - Bollenbach.
newsitem.headline: Hilton to pursue Asia-Pacific expansion - Bollenbach.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp, soon to be the biggest hotelier in the United States, said on Monday it plans to expand in the Asia-Pacific after regaining the right to use its brand name overseas after a 32-year hiatus.
Hilton Hotels unveiled a plan late last month to pay roughly US$180 million to acquire five percent of Ladbroke Group PLC, which owns the Hilton name overseas.
Now the group is setting its sights firmly on using its name throughout the Asia-Pacific, a region considered one of the fastest growing for the hotel industry globally.

"We haven't spent enough time looking for opportunities, and one of the reasons is because we didn't have the right to use the Hilton name overseas, so we concentrated on our interests in the United States," said Stephen Bollenbach, Hilton chief executive, during a visit to Hong Kong on Monday.
Ladbroke and Hilton have agreed to form a separate company to unify the operations, marketing and development of all Hilton hotels, giving them control of more than 400 hotels in 49 countries.

Bollenbach said Hilton Hotels, which has used the Conrad Hotels brand name overseas, would now consider using the Hilton name in China which boasts growth rates in its hotel industry among the biggest in the region.
"We are looking at China very carefully," Bollenbach said.
The Hilton brand has been split since Hilton spun off its overseas operations in 1964, forming Hilton International. Labroke acquired Hilton International in 1987.
Bollenbach said the deal would not mean structural changes in Asia, where Hilton has no plans to rename its current Conrad properties.
While the deal gives Hilton a bigger stake in the international hotel business, it allows Ladbroke the opportunity to participate in Hilton's growing gambling presence in the United States.

But Bollenbach said opportunites to expand its gaming empire in Southeast Asia were limited. "There are not many places in Southeast Asia that allow casino gaming and we're not in the business of persuading governments to allow it. We're not political advocates," he said.
